evaluations.label: A
errors: "kick off TS3012a, a project" - no project name or code is mentioned anywhere in the transcript.
Project manager is called "Markoff" throughout; he introduces himself as Mark.
Industrial designer is called "Savier" / "Savier Jokins"; the transcript has Xavier Juergens.
User interface designer is called "Speaker 4" although he introduced himself as Nick Broer.
"Speaker 4 clarifies that the scope of the project is limited to a TV remote control" - the UI designer asked the question; the project manager answered that the brief was for a TV remote only.
Lists "Should the device be designed as a multi-remote control or limited strictly to television functions?" as an open question; it was answered in the meeting (TV only).
"Savier Jokins suggests using lightweight materials that are aesthetically impactful" - he only said the material should be light; nothing about aesthetic impact.
Next steps omit that the personal coach, not the project manager, hands out the personal assignments.
strengths: Broadest coverage: roles, three questions for the industrial designer (paraphrased), three-phase process, whiteboard training, project folder, animal exercise, scope, accessibility, material, prices, 30-minute reconvene.
Captures the price targets (25 euros selling, 12.50 production) correctly.
Readable structure with summary, outline and open questions.
weaknesses: Invents a project code and misspells or mislabels three of four participants.
Misattributes the scope clarification and lists a settled point as open.
Action items are generic restatements of the brief with no owners, and miss the only concrete commitment (marketing expert to bring ideas).
Omits that the marketing expert had nothing ready yet and that the whiteboard was found unresponsive.

evaluations.label: B
errors: Action item owner written as "Dirk Mengveld"; the transcript has Dirk Meinfeld (minor spelling).

"The interface designer urged familiarity and rational changes" - the transcript line is garbled ("No rational changes or whatever, 'cause it revolutionary changes, yes"); the direction of the second half is uncertain, so "rational changes" is a guess.
Several timestamps are a few seconds early relative to the transcript (e.g. scope at [11:32] vs 11:25-11:34, lightweight material at [12:35] vs [12:33]); not materially misleading.
strengths: Names Mark, Dirk and Xavier correctly and attributes statements to the right people throughout.
Correctly states the scope decision (TV only), the price targets, the lightweight-material point, the accessibility discussion and the 30-minute reconvene with assignments from the personal coach.
Only set that records the marketing expert had no ideas ready yet and turns that into the one real action item with an owner.
Captures the whiteboard responsiveness complaint and the pen-and-paper preference.
Clear summary up top plus timestamped detail someone could check.
weaknesses: Omits the industrial designer's three guiding questions (what happens inside, what it is made of, what it looks like).
Never names the user interface designer (Nick Broer) even though he introduced himself.
Slight over-interpretation of the elephant as chosen "as a market image"; the market framing came from Mark, not Dirk.

evaluations.label: C
errors: "Mark Knopp" - the project manager gives only his first name; no surname appears in the transcript.
"Xavier Juukens" and "Dirk Mankveld" - transcript has Xavier Juergens and Dirk Meinfeld.
"Provide personal assignments to team members" assigned to Mark - the project manager said the personal coach will give the assignments.

"Address material considerations for lightweight design" assigned to Xavier and "Prepare intuitive design concepts" assigned to the UI designer - no such assignments were made in the meeting; these are inferred.
"Dolphin: freedom, smooth design" - nothing about smooth design was said; the dolphin stood for freedom, the ocean and swimming.
Timestamps are often off: scope clarification marked (10:34) actually occurs at 11:25-11:34; pricing marked (12:10) occurs at 12:43; assignments marked (13:53) is past the end of the transcript.
strengths: Compact and scannable; hits the main points (scope TV only, intuitive, accessible, light, 25 / 12.5 euro prices, 30-minute break).
Records that the marketing expert will bring input later.
weaknesses: Invents surnames and invents action items with owners that were never assigned, which could send people off doing the wrong work.
Wrongly credits Mark with handing out personal assignments.
Skips the team introductions and roles, including the industrial designer's three questions.
Too terse for someone who missed the meeting to understand context (who is who, why the animals were drawn).

evaluations.label: D
errors: "Mark Knopf" - no surname is given in the transcript.
"Dirk Mengveld" and "Xavier Jökens" - transcript has Dirk Meinfeld and Xavier Juergens (spelling).
"UI designer also present (name not captured)" - he introduced himself as Nick Broer.
"Dolphin: freedom, openness" - "openness" is not in the transcript (freedom, ocean, swimming were).
"Tiger: speed, efficiency, security, precision" - "precision" is a stretch of "well-thought way"; minor.
"rational changes only" repeats the garbled transcript line as if it were a clear statement.
strengths: Accurate on all the substantive points: TV-only scope, intuitive/familiar design, accessibility consideration, lightweight material, 25 / 12.50 euro prices, three phases, project folder, 30-minute reconvene with assignments from the personal coach.
Only set besides A to record the industrial designer's three questions, and it lists them verbatim.
Captures the tight-budget remark and the distinct-from-competitors takeaway.
Short, well organised, easy to act on.
weaknesses: No action items or owners; misses that the marketing expert had nothing ready and will bring ideas later.
Invents a surname for Mark and fails to name the UI designer.

rationale: B is the most reliable: correct first names, correct attribution of who asked versus who decided, all key numbers and decisions, and the one genuine follow-up (Dirk to bring marketing ideas) captured as an owned action item; its only gaps are the industrial designer's three questions and the UI designer's name. D is nearly as accurate and includes the three questions, but has no action items, invents a surname and misses the marketing expert's pending ideas. A covers the most ground but invents a project code, garbles or omits most names, misattributes the scope clarification to the UI designer, lists the settled multi-remote question as open, and offers only generic unowned action items. C is terse and invents the most consequential content: surnames, three action items that were never assigned, and credits Mark with handing out assignments that the personal coach gives, so someone acting on it could do the wrong work.
